official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory consultee role
official_measurement_examples.fact: National Highways is a statutory consultee where proposals may affect safety, queuing, maintenance or access to the Strategic Road Network; consultation is not planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Direct access distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A proposal involving a new or altered access to the SRN requires specific assessment; proximity to an SRN road is not evidence of a lawful direct access right.

official_measurement_examples.name: Capacity assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: Transport Assessment and modelling evidence is proposal and scenario specific; a network model or current spare capacity is not a permanent capacity reservation.

official_measurement_examples.name: RIS3 investment context
official_measurement_examples.fact: RIS3 covers 2026 to 2031 investment in the SRN but inclusion of a road scheme or corridor does not grant planning permission to a nearby parcel or guarantee a delivery date for enabling works.

official_measurement_examples.name: Mitigation distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A requirement for mitigation or highway works can be a planning consideration or condition, but identifying mitigation does not prove it is funded, permitted or delivered.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local and strategic networks
official_measurement_examples.fact: The SRN is distinct from local highway networks; National Highways authority status does not substitute for the relevant local highway authority on local roads.

official_measurement_examples.name: Accelerator fund limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: National Highways growth-fund eligibility requires advanced schemes and transport improvements but fund eligibility or support is not planning permission or a capacity guarantee.

official_measurement_examples.name: Transport evidence limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Transport evidence supports planning judgment and cumulative-impact assessment but does not determine land ownership, title access rights or final parcel yield.

core_rules: National Highways consultation is not planning permission
SRN proximity is not a lawful access right
transport model output is not permanent network capacity
RIS3 investment is not parcel permission
mitigation identification is not mitigation delivery
SRN and local highway authority roles remain distinct
fund eligibility is not planning permission
route strategy is not site allocation
planning condition is not completed highway work
transport evidence does not determine land ownership
network capacity does not determine parcel yield
no parcel highway clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official National Highways, DfT, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. Current National Highways planning service and RIS3 2026-31 context retained with consultation, access, capacity, mitigation and permission separation; no parcel promotion.
